## FEED OPTIMIZATION

### What Google-Owned Sources Support
- Product data must accurately represent the product and match the landing page.
- GTIN and other identifiers should be submitted when they actually exist for the product.
- Feed freshness, price accuracy, availability accuracy, checkout consistency, and image quality are compliance and eligibility concerns before they are optimization levers.
- Retail Performance Max and Shopping diagnostics should start with Merchant Center linkage, product-data status, product issues, and the campaign's current Shopping or Performance Max setup.
- AI Max for Shopping is a beta feature family. Treat AI Max for Shopping text customization, final URL expansion, reporting, and optimization guidance as account-eligibility and rollout-sensitive until current Help/account evidence proves availability.

### Practical Feed Priorities
1. Fix mismatches between feed data and landing pages first.
2. Fill required and high-signal attributes before chasing title experiments.
3. Keep update cadence aligned to how often price, availability, or key attributes really change.
4. Use custom labels for business slicing and bidding logic, not as a ranking guarantee by themselves.
5. When AI Max for Shopping is enabled, allow enough ramp-up before making control changes and use product-title, asset, landing-page, and search-term reporting as diagnostic surfaces rather than deterministic targeting levers.

### Safe Optimization Guidance
- Product titles should help Google and shoppers identify the item clearly, but there is no single universal title formula that overrides the underlying product data requirements.
- Feed work affects eligibility, matching, and click quality, but do not promise fixed CTR or ROAS lifts from one attribute change.
- Treat Merchant Center diagnostics and product-data specification docs as the canonical source before quoting image or attribute rules.
- Treat GML / I/O commerce announcements such as Universal Commerce Protocol, Universal Cart, and agentic checkout as strategic commerce context unless a current Google Ads Help or API source ties the feature to an advertiser control.

### What Not To Present As Fact
- Do not quote generic GTIN or title-lift percentages as universal platform outcomes.
- Do not imply that custom labels directly improve auction rank by themselves.
- Do not treat feed-policy compliance as optional clean-up; it is part of the serving contract.
- Do not invent a separate checkout-driven Shopping score, lower-CPC, or fixed-lift mechanism unless Google publishes the exact current mechanism in a primary source.
- Do not imply every retail account can use AI Max for Shopping or agentic checkout features today.
